concepts.title: Concept of Human Capital and People as Resource

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Concept of Human Capital and People as Resource' refers to.
questions.a: The working segment of a country considered in terms of its skills, technical abilities, and productive capacities that contribute to national output.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Concept of Human Capital and People as Resource'.
questions.a: Investing in human beings turns population from a liability into a productive economic asset.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Concept of Human Capital and People as Resource' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Overview (source: iess202.txt lines 1-60)

concepts.title: Virtuous and Vicious Cycles in Human Capital Formation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Virtuous and Vicious Cycles in Human Capital Formation' refers to.
questions.a: A developmental pattern where educated parents invest substantially in their children creating positive compounding gains, contrasted with disadvantaged parents perpetuating deprivation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Virtuous and Vicious Cycles in Human Capital Formation'.
questions.a: Sustained family investment in child health and learning creates intergenerational upward mobility.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Virtuous and Vicious Cycles in Human Capital Formation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Story of Sakal and Vilas (source: iess202.txt lines 61-160)

concepts.title: Classification of Economic Activities into Three Sectors

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classification of Economic Activities into Three Sectors' refers to.
questions.a: The categorisation of all output generating activities into primary extraction, secondary manufacturing, and tertiary service provision.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification of Economic Activities into Three Sectors'.
questions.a: All three sectors jointly contribute goods and services to the Gross National Product.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Classification of Economic Activities into Three Sectors' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Economic Activities by Men and Women (source: iess202.txt lines 161-200)

concepts.title: Market versus Non-Market Activities and Gender Division of Labour

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Market versus Non-Market Activities and Gender Division of Labour' refers to.
questions.a: The distinction between tasks performed for remuneration or profit and unpaid tasks performed for self consumption or domestic upkeep.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Market versus Non-Market Activities and Gender Division of Labour'.
questions.a: Unpaid household work by women is excluded from national income calculations due to the non-market nature of domestic chores.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Market versus Non-Market Activities and Gender Division of Labour' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Economic Activities by Men and Women (source: iess202.txt lines 201-260)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Education and Quality of Population' refers to.
questions.a: The development of human knowledge, values, and literacy that improves individual earning potential and strengthens social governance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Education and Quality of Population'.
questions.a: Universal elementary education policies like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Mid-Day Meals improve school retention and literacy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Education and Quality of Population' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Quality of Population - Education (source: iess202.txt lines 261-360)

questions.q: Using the method 'Health Indicators and Human Development', work with: val_final = 8, val_initial = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pct_change.
questions.a: 98.4 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Health Indicators and Human Development' and work with: val_final = 50, val_initial = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pct_change.
questions.a: 75 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Health Indicators and Human Development' refers to.
questions.a: The physiological well-being of the population measured through statistical indicators like life expectancy, infant mortality rate, crude birth rate, and crude death rate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Health Indicators and Human Development'.
questions.a: A healthy workforce maximizes output and prevents loss of working potential due to illness.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Health Indicators and Human Development', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: imr = (infant_deaths / live_births) * 1000

questions.q: Using the method 'Unemployment and Workforce Demographics', work with: employed_count = 24, labour_force = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployment_rate.
questions.a: 84 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Unemployment and Workforce Demographics' and work with: employed_count = 40, labour_force = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployment_rate.
questions.a: 20 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unemployment and Workforce Demographics' refers to.
questions.a: A condition in which individuals within the active working age bracket who are seeking employment at prevailing wages cannot secure jobs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unemployment and Workforce Demographics'.
questions.a: Only individuals aged 15 to 59 years actively seeking paid work are counted in unemployment statistics.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Unemployment and Workforce Demographics', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: unemployed_count = labour_force - employed_count

concepts.title: Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated

questions.q: Using the method 'Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated', work with: required_workers = 25000, total_workers = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of surplus_labour.
questions.a: -22500 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated' and work with: required_workers = 12000, total_workers = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of surplus_labour.
questions.a: -9500 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated' refers to.
questions.a: Distinct forms of joblessness including agricultural off-season idleness, invisible surplus workers on family plots, and educated degree holders lacking suitable jobs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated'.
questions.a: Disguised unemployment occurs when marginal productivity of surplus workers is zero.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: surplus_labour = total_workers - required_workers

concepts.title: Consequences of Unemployment and Sectoral Absorption

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consequences of Unemployment and Sectoral Absorption' refers to.
questions.a: The socio-economic costs of joblessness that transform assets into liabilities, increase dependency ratios, and prompt labour migration to secondary and tertiary sectors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consequences of Unemployment and Sectoral Absorption'.
questions.a: Unemployment increases economic overload and leads to loss of human capital potential.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Consequences of Unemployment and Sectoral Absorption' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Unemployment / Story of a Village (source: iess202.txt lines 541-620)
